_comment: Static facts about Mumbai's seven supply lakes. Capacities are BMC useful storage in ML (sum = 14,47,363 ML). Build years, supply (MLD), treatment plants and areas served come from a Citizen Matters explainer and must be verified against BMC before release. Coordinates are APPROXIMATE (dam/lake area) and should be replaced with OpenStreetMap geometry.
sources: https://www.mumbailakewaterlevel.in (capacities, BMC Hydraulic Engineer's Dept. figures)

Mumbai 1.serves: Western suburbs (Dahisar Check Naka to Bandra) and the western island city (Mahim to Malabar Hill)

Mumbai 2.serves: Eastern suburbs (Mulund Check Naka to Sion) and Sion to Mazgaon

lakes.name: Bhatsa
lakes.built_note: Built by the Maharashtra government at the confluence of the Bhatsa and Chorana rivers; the largest of the seven.

lakes.name: Upper Vaitarna
lakes.built_note: State multipurpose scheme with dams on the Vaitarna and Alwandi rivers; water is used for power generation before release into Modak Sagar.

lakes.name: Middle Vaitarna
lakes.position_note: Dam location (Wikipedia, Middle Vaitarna Dam). No reservoir outline yet: not in OpenStreetMap; India-WRIS water bodies is a candidate source.
lakes.built_note: Most recent of the seven, built by BMC on the Vaitarna.

lakes.name: Modak Sagar (Lower Vaitarna)
lakes.built_note: Named after N. V. Modak, BMC's chief engineer at the time.

lakes.name: Tansa
lakes.built_note: Construction began in 1886 and was completed in four stages by 1945.

lakes.name: Vihar
lakes.built_note: Dam at the source of the Mithi river; completed by 1860.

lakes.name: Tulsi
lakes.built_note: Dam completed in 1872 across the Tassu river; became an independent reservoir in 1877. The smallest of the seven; overflow runs into Vihar.
